blocks.summary: Set up a project once, then write JSON pages. Every page is a tree of kind-tagged blocks; this page documents the kinds (inline, prose, emphasis, layout, visual), how to thread them together, per-page metadata, and the build outputs.

blocks.title: Project setup
blocks.lead: One-time per project. Links the kit so pages can reference _kit/chrome.js and friends without copying anything.

blocks.source:
cd path/to/your-project/docs
html-doc init     # creates _kit symlink + index.html in cwd

# Optional: drop a starter page into the docs root
# (The starter pair ships inside the html_doc package — for a
# git checkout it lives at src/html_doc/templates/starter.json.)

cd ..
html-doc serve    # http://localhost:9876 with live reload

blocks.title: Relative .md links rewrite to .html
blocks.content: [overview](other.md#section) in a Markdown page becomes other.html#section at render time, so links between .md pages work the same as between .json pages. Absolute URLs (http, https, mailto), fragment-only refs (#section), and absolute paths (/x) pass through unchanged.

blocks.title: Every Markdown file is a page by default
blocks.content: README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, LICENSE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, SECURITY.md and any other .md the walker reaches all surface as pages. Hide one by moving it under a SKIP_DIRS subdirectory (dist/, _kit/, .git/, .venv/, node_modules/, templates/, _internal/). Missing Markdown features (nested lists, footnotes, definition lists, reference-style links, inline HTML pass-through, YAML front-matter) are tracked in P4 of the roadmap.

blocks.content: First-class JSON table. Two shapes: flat rows or grouped groups. Renders into a real <table> plus a runtime control bar (filter input, stats counter, Table / List / Cards view toggle, sticky header, full-width auto-fit). Object-form headers and cells declare chip filters with multi-valued cells; groups are collapsible.

Headers can declare a fixed chip set with filter: "chips"; cells use the object form { value, values } to belong to one or more chip values. AND across columns, OR within a column. Combine with the text filter.

blocks.title: Board view: kanban lanes in declared order

blocks.content: Set view: "board" on the table block to open in kanban lanes by default — rows become cards in one lane per unique value of the group column. Declare boardOrder on the column header to force the lane sequence; without it, lanes appear in first-occurrence order, which rarely matches the kanban flow you want. Values present in row data but missing from boardOrder render at the end so authors can spot the omission. The other views (Table / List / Cards) are still one click away in the view toggle.

code.source:
{
  "kind": "table",
  "view": "board",
  "headers": [
    "Item",
    { "label": "Status",
      "boardOrder": ["queued", "in-progress", "blocked", "done"] }
  ],
  "rows": [
    ["Cut release tag",        "queued"],
    ["Wire CI matrix",         "in-progress"],
    ["Vendor security review", "blocked"],
    ["Migrate auth layer",     "done"],
    ["Draft RFC",              "in-progress"],
    ["Update changelog",       "queued"]
  ]
}

blocks.title: Visual primitives
blocks.lead: chart, diagram, live-snippet — the rich content primitives that justify the JSON-source choice over Markdown.

content: Single primitive, many render modes via the

renders a distribution arc. The renderer dispatches by
— each mode has its own payload shape; unused fields are ignored.

blocks.title: Library underneath
blocks.content: All modes are kit-native — no third-party chart library. Cartesian + donut modes render as inline SVG drawn by the html-doc-chart Custom Element. The bar family renders as plain HTML + CSS, no JavaScript after first paint.

The 22 chart variants group into seven families. Pick by what you're communicating; the variants inside a family share scaffolding (axes, hover, legend) so swapping between them is a one-field change.

cards.title: Categorical
cards.content: One value per category. Sort by value for ranking, by name for lookup.
items: type: bar — horizontal bars, baseline-zero, supports a display override.
type: stacked-bar — same row, multiple stacked segments.
type: grouped-bar — same row, side-by-side mini-bars.
type: waffle — N×M cell grid; each cell is one unit.

cards.title: Distribution
cards.content: Shape of one variable. Use when the spread / skew is the story, not a single number.
items: type: ridgeline — stacked small-distributions with a parallel cursor.

cards.title: Time series
cards.content: X is time (or any ordered axis). Use line when each x has one y; area when stacking matters.
items: type: line — connected y vs x.
type: area — line with fill below.

cards.title: Hierarchy / share
cards.content: Parts of a whole. Donut for ≤6 slices; treemap when nesting or many cells beat slices.
items: type: donut — distribution arc with centre total.

cards.title: Relationship
cards.content: Two or more variables interacting. Scatter for raw points; heatmap when density beats individual points.
items: type: scatter — y vs x points, optional series.
type: bubble — scatter with a third (size) variable.
type: quadrant — scatter with cross-hair guide + corner labels.

cards.title: Goal / comparison
cards.content: Actual vs target — the visual answers 'are we there yet?'
items: type: bullet — single actual against bands.
type: gauge — single value as a 0→max arc.

cards.title: Conversion
cards.content: Stage-to-stage drop-off through an ordered pipeline.
items: type: funnel — narrowing bands per stage with aligned label / value / % columns.

cards.title: Flow
cards.content: Where the flow goes — links between nodes carry magnitude.
items: type: sankey — left-to-right ribbons sized by link value, with column-stacked nodes.

cards.title: Graph
cards.content: Connections between entities. Node degree drives circle radius.
items: type: network — force-relaxed node-link diagram for small graphs (≤ ~50 nodes).

cards.title: Multivariate
cards.content: Many variables at once — when the story lives in correlations, not totals.
items: type: scatter-matrix — N×N grid of mini scatters; diagonal labels each axis.
type: parallel-coordinates — one vertical axis per variable; each record draws a polyline crossing them.

cards.title: Relationship · circular
cards.content: Pairwise flow / affinity between a small group of entities.
items: type: chord — perimeter arcs sized by total flow, ribbons through the middle for each pair.

cards.title: Geographic
cards.content: Country / region comparison without map-tile data.
items: type: geo — tile cartogram with one cell per ISO region code, coloured by value, scaled in a sequential ramp.

blocks.content: One or more series of {x, y} points. Per-point label optional (shown on hover). Per-series colour drawn from the accent / warn / danger / success / muted vocabulary. Axes auto-scale; pass x-scale=log / y-scale=log on the element for log axes.

content: Row-per-item horizontal bars. Each row carries
caps the bar full-width; if omitted, the largest row's value sets the scale. Use when you want a label/value comparison without axis chrome.

blocks.content: Same shape as line — series of {x, y} points — but the curve is filled down to the baseline. Useful for cumulative metrics over time where magnitude matters as much as direction.

content: Scatter plot with a third dimension encoded as dot size. Each point gains an optional
field; the renderer takes its square root so the dot's AREA is proportional to size (eye reads area, not radius). Useful for cost vs. impact vs. confidence-style decision matrices.

render.title: Initiatives — cost vs. impact vs. team-size

content: Scatter plot split into four regions by two reference lines. Author supplies a
(horizontal split) and optionally four corner labels (
). Reads as a 2×2 decision matrix at a glance.
Multi-series horizontal bars where each row's series stack into a single bar. Author supplies
. The right-hand readout is the row total. Use for breakdown-of-a-total visualisation.

blocks.content: Same payload as stacked-bar, but each series renders as its own thin sub-bar within the row rather than stacking. Use for direct comparison across series within the same category.

content: ; the renderer normalises values to percentages of the total, draws an arc per slice, and shows the total + a legend on the side.

blocks.content: N×M cell grid coloured by value. `cells` is a 2D array (outer = rows, inner = columns). Optional `row_labels` / `col_labels` annotate the edges. `scale` picks the palette family: sequential (one-sided ramp on accent) or diverging (accent for positives, danger for negatives). Hover any cell for the raw value.

Inline mini line / area / bar. No axes, no chrome — sized for the line height of surrounding prose. `values` is a flat numeric series. `variant` picks line (default), area (filled), or bar (per-value mini-bars). `end_label` renders to the right of the curve as a small caption (`62%`, `↗`, etc.).

Dot-matrix breakdown. Default 10×10 grid (= 100 cells). `segments` is a list of `{label, count, color}`; the renderer fills cells in order, one per unit count. The legend lives to the right of the grid with the percentage of each segment.

Semicircular arc, 0 → max, with a needle / fill at the current value and an optional target tick. Use for single-metric status (SLO budget, runway, uptime) where the gap to target is the point. Optional `zones` paint coloured threshold bands behind the value.

N spokes radiating from centre, one filled polygon per series. Best for 3–8 axes and 1–4 series. `axes[].label` names the spoke; optional `axes[].max` overrides per-axis scaling. `series[].values` array must align with `axes` by index.
Quartiles + whiskers + optional outliers — one row per `boxes[]` entry. Required: `min`, `q1`, `median`, `q3`, `max`. Optional: `outliers: [Number]` rendered as dots beyond the whiskers.

Actual-vs-target on a banded horizontal track — Stephen Few's bullet chart. One row per `tracks[]` entry: `label`, `value` (current), `target` (optional vertical tick), `max` (right-edge), optional `zones` painted behind the value.

Two-time-point change — left column is `from`, right column is `to`, one slope line per `items[]` entry. The renderer auto-colours rising as success and falling as danger unless an explicit `color` is set. Use this when ‘who went up, who went down’ is the question.

Frequency by bin. Author supplies the binning (`bins[]` with `{lo, hi, count}`). Contiguous bins read as a connected distribution; gaps are allowed but render with the visible gap. Use for distribution shape, latency tail, time-to-event.

Year-in-cells activity grid. `date_values` is a map of ISO date → numeric value; days missing from the map render faintly to show the calendar shape. Mon, Wed, Fri labels along the left; month names along the top at the first cell of each month.

Area-proportional nested rectangles via squarified layout. `tree[]` is a flat list of `{label, value, color?}` leaves; the largest values occupy the largest rectangles. Labels render only when the rectangle is large enough to fit them legibly. Use for composition (LoC by language, spend by category, traffic by route).

Stacked small-distributions, one per row. `distributions[].values` is a flat sample; the renderer bins each sample into ~30 buckets over the global range. Read for shape comparison across groups (per-region latency, per-cohort engagement).

Conversion-stage drop-off. `stages[]` is an ordered list of `{label, value, color?}`. The renderer draws a tapered band between adjacent stages; the right-hand readout shows the value + percentage of the first stage.

Flow between stages with curved ribbons sized by link value. nodes[] is {id, label?, color?}; links[] is {source, target, value} referencing node ids. The renderer derives the left-to-right column placement from the link graph (BFS depth), stacks nodes within each column by their incoming-or-outgoing total, and routes a cubic-Bezier ribbon between every pair.

Node-link diagram with a small Fruchterman-Reingold-ish force relaxation (~60 iterations on each render). Best for graphs up to ~50 nodes — bigger structures need a real graph-viz library. nodes[] + links[] share the same shape as sankey. Node radius scales with degree; hovering a node surfaces its label + degree in the tooltip.

N×N grid of mini scatter plots for multivariate correlation reading. variables[] defines each axis; records[] is a flat list of objects keyed by variable id. The diagonal cells show the variable name; off-diagonal cells plot var-col vs var-row. Domains auto-derive from the records unless declared explicitly.

One vertical axis per variable; each record draws a polyline crossing all axes at its scaled position. Best for spotting multi-variable clusters (lines that bunch together) or outliers (lines that diverge). Optional _label and _color on each record tag it visually.

Circular relationship diagram. groups[] defines the perimeter sequence (clockwise from 12 o'clock); matrix is an N×N flow matrix where matrix[i][j] is the flow from groups[i] to groups[j]. Each group occupies an outer arc sized by its total in+out flow; ribbons through the centre carry the pairwise flows.

Tile cartogram. regions[] is a list of {id, value, label?} where id is an ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 country code (US, GB, DE, BR, ...) or the synthetic OTH bucket. The kit ships a fixed tile grid (~60 cells) that approximates a flat world map; absent regions render as faint placeholder outlines so the geography stays visible. Cell fill scales with value in a single-hue sequential ramp.

blocks.title: Per-page metadata
blocks.lead: meta drives nav placement, the cover header, the llms.txt sitemap, and search excerpts.

cards.title: Display fields
content: eyebrow — small label above the H1 ("Architecture", "Notes").
subtitle — one-paragraph description under the H1.
date — ISO date or human string. Shown in cover meta.
read_time — like "~5 min read". Shown in cover meta.

cards.title: Behavior fields
content: order — sort key in the site-tree nav. Lower = earlier.
summary — one line. Used in nav tooltips, llms.txt, search.
lang — "en" or "tr" (or any code the kit knows). Overrides the project default.
accent (top-level, not under meta) — named token or CSS color.

content.content: The kit doesn't parse the date — it's a display string. Use whatever convention you've adopted (ISO 8601, locale date). For consistency across a project, pick one and stick. Sort order in the nav uses meta.order, not the date.

blocks.title: Build outputs
blocks.lead: html-doc build produces three trees under dist/, one per audience. Authors don't need to run it during dev — the runtime renderer fetches JSON directly — but build is required for search, the standalone single-file mode, and the llms.txt sitemap.

steps.title: dist/site/
steps.content: Deployable multi-page site. Every HTML + JSON copied with directory structure preserved. Kit assets bundled at dist/site/_kit/. site-manifest.json sits at the docs root for the runtime page-nav fetch. Drop on any static host.

steps.title: dist/standalone/
steps.content: Single-file artifacts. Every HTML inlines kit JS, CSS, page JSON, glossary bundle, and the manifest as window.__htmldocManifest. One self-contained file per page that opens offline — email-as-attachment ready. No sidecar manifest or llms.txt needed.

steps.title: dist/markdown/
steps.content: page.md twin for every JSON page + a single llms.txt sitemap (one line per page: URL + title + summary, convention from llmstxt.org). Single canonical home — no duplication across the human trees.

blocks.title: Pagefind search — optional dependency
blocks.content: If pagefind is on PATH (brew install pagefind, or npx pagefind), build also indexes dist/site/ into dist/site/pagefind/. Soft-fails without it. The search button in the chrome only works on built sites.

blocks.title: Layout / chrome — not in the page JSON
blocks.lead: page-chrome, page-nav, page-toc are set in the HTML stub, not the page JSON. The stub copy-pastes from src/html_doc/templates/starter.html and you usually don't touch it.

items: — system cluster top-right (search, warning, theme cycler). Edge tabs for sidebars. Visual Viewport pinch-zoom tracker.

— boxed site-tree at the top of the single left sidebar; reads site-manifest.json (or the inline window.__htmldocManifest in standalone builds). Marks the active page. Right-edge handle resizes / collapses. Footer at the bottom carries the kit version.

— section-TOC stacked under the site tree inside the same left sidebar. Heading reflects the current page title; the list is built from main > section > h2/h3 after the renderer fires html-doc:rendered.

blocks.title: Cross-cutting features
blocks.lead: Behaviors that don't introduce a new block kind but change how an existing one renders.

blocks.content: Existing ext-ref entries auto-promote to type-themed citation cards (paper / rfc / release / blog / other). Type is read from the extref entry or inferred from the link domain. Inline cite text inherits the type's color on its dotted underline; the hover card carries a type-tinted icon, a mono domain pill, optional author + date row, and a summary.

blocks.content: Add bind: "step-3" to any two blocks and they flash together when either is hovered or focused. Click one — the offscreen partner scrolls into view. One-line opt-in per pair; no kind change required.
Inline sample — hover or focus this paragraph and the callout below tints in sync. They share the same data-bind key.

blocks.title: Paired callout
blocks.content: Hovering the paragraph above lights this callout's border. Hovering this callout lights the paragraph. Same key, both directions.
meta.updated renders as a quiet italic line under the cover meta row. Pure trust signal — readers learn at a glance how fresh a page is.

Callout type accepts both the kit's original names (warn / warning / danger / success / neutral) and the industry-standard aliases (note / tip / info / caution). Each row below is the same canonical styling reached from two different vocabularies.

blocks.title: note · alias of neutral
blocks.content: type: "note" reads the same as type: "neutral" — generic informational tint.

blocks.title: tip · alias of success
blocks.content: type: "tip" matches type: "success" — green guidance accent for positive advice.

blocks.title: info · alias of neutral with informational tint
blocks.content: Same surface as neutral; reserved name keeps Docusaurus / Mintlify habits intact.

blocks.title: caution · alias of warning
blocks.content: Amber border + icon; same look as type: "warning" from earlier rounds.
